text:
sarah: Quick async update on Optimize toolkit delivery — putting this here so folks can pick up without meetings.
sarah: Summary: pushed quantization recommendations for mistral-7b-v2 and batching/caching suggestions into the optkit repo. Need owners for: regression smoke, runtime kernel flag, and canary rollout plan.
sarah: Key points: 8-bit GPTQ shows ~1.6x throughput, ~7% median quality delta on our eval set. KV-prefix caching gives big latency wins for short prompt tails. Batching defaults too aggressive for <64-token tails; recommending dynamic_batch_size = 8 for low-p99 latency.
kai: Thanks — where's the PR? can you drop the link?
sarah: https://github.com/redwood/optkit/pull/432 (diff has perf table + config snippets)
maria: I can own regression smoke for the eval harness. quick question: which prompt sets to run? full-squad or a reduced 10k seed?
ian: we should run both. reduced 10k first for fast feedback, then full-squad overnight if the 10k passes.
ian: also flag: eng-runtime needs a small patch to expose dynamic_batch_size via the router config. i've got a draft branch (runtime/dyn-batch-expose).
kai: who can land the runtime patch? we need that before canary.
ian: i'll finish the patch today and open a PR; @sarah can you update the optkit PR to point at the runtime branch for integration tests?
sarah: yep, i'll update the PR after ian's PR is up.
alex: perf ask: can we get the p50/p95/p99 numbers for the 8-bit vs fp16 on the ml-infer cluster? want to estimate cost delta.
sarah: short numbers from my local runs: fp16 p50=82ms p95=210ms p99=430ms; 8-bit p50=52ms p95=140ms p99=320ms. these are with KV cache enabled and batch size tuned.
alex: nice. please surface token/sec and GPU utilization in the PR tables too.
sarah: will do.
deploy-bot: build status for optkit PR 432: CI unit tests passed. integration smoke queued (runner: eng-runtime-integ-2). :white_check_mark:
maria: once CI for integration passes, i'll run reduced-10k eval and share diffs. if we see >3% quality regression on any intent bucket, hold canary.
kai: ownership: regression smoke -> maria; runtime patch -> ian; canary plan + rollout doc -> sarah; infra quota check for canary GPUs -> alex. agreed?
ian: agreed. i'll ping the eng-sre channel for a quick quota check as soon as PR lands.
sarah: action items summarized:
- ian: PR to expose dynamic_batch_size (ETA today)
- sarah: update optkit PR to point at runtime branch + add token/sec table (ETA EOD)
- maria: run reduced-10k eval after integ CI (ETA tomorrow morning)
- alex: confirm GPU quota for canary (ETA today)
- kai: coordinate canary timing with product (ETA after eval pass)

sarah: small snippet for suggested default config in optkit (copy-paste):
```yaml
model: mistral-7b-v2
quant: gptq-8bit
dynamic_batch_size: 8
kv_cache_enabled: true
```
sarah: ping me if anyone wants me to pair on the eval harness run. otherwise i'll post results in this thread and update the PR description.
kai: awesome — will follow up after maria posts results. :thumbsup:
maria: starting reduced-10k now, will post diff link when ready.
ian: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/289 — contains flag + unit tests. cc @kai @sarah
sarah: got it, thanks ian. updating optkit PR to reference runtime/pr-289 now.
deploy-bot: integration smoke for optkit PR 432 started on eng-runtime-integ-2 at 2026-03-17T18:12:05Z.
maria: reduced-10k done — no bucket >2.1% regression. posting results: https://ci.redwood/evals/optkit/432/reduced-10k (summary table in PR comments)
kai: good signal. next: determine canary window. product prefers low-traffic window: sat 02:00-05:00 UTC. can we do that?
alex: quota check: we have 8 GPUs available in region-us-west for that window, can run canary 4-instance setup.
sarah: i'll draft the canary runbook and update the rollout doc. thanks all — i'll close block once canary is scheduled.
ian: leaving a note: if runtime PR lands after EOD, we may need to delay canary by 24h for infra to pick up new image; keeping timeline flexible.
kai: noted. folks, if anything urgent ping me but otherwise let's keep async here. :pray:
